views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Engage the rescheduled October high-level talks in Washington seriously and constructively, holding the existing 25%/15% tariff structure as leverage while signaling a genuine openness to de-escalation. Do not escalate further — the Oct 1 hike to 30% was already delayed to Oct 15 as a goodwill gesture, and Beijing has reciprocated with its first exemption lists (including soybeans and pork). Use this window to lock in a deal that protects the farm belt and rebuilds export access without sacrificing the structural IP/enforcement gains already locked down.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is moderate-positive (+0.35), not existential. The US holds the tactical advantage — it is on offense with 25% tariffs on ~$250B and 15% on List 4A (Sept 1) in place, the broad dollar index is strong (116.9, +2.2% since spring), and China is blinking first (Sept 5 agreement to resume talks; Sept 11 Trump deferred the Oct 1 hike at Liu He's request; Sept 13 Beijing exempting soy/pork). But the dispute is visibly biting the real economy: the 10Y yield has collapsed from ~2.5% to 1.80% with the curve flat/near-inverted (a classic recession signal), consumer sentiment dropped from 100 (May) to 89.8 (Aug), and the Federal Reserve has cut the funds rate from 2.42% to 2.04%. The sharpest vulnerability is the farm belt — soybean exports to China fell roughly three-quarters, China bought only about half the soybeans it pledged, and Senators like Grassley warn farmers are 'at risk of permanently losing an export market' — a live 2020 re-election concern in battleground states. Escalating further would deepen that farm damage and amplify recession risk at exactly the moment Beijing is offering concessions. Conversely, a full concession would waste the leverage already built. The calibrated move is to negotiate: convert Beijing's goodwill and the scheduled talks into enforceable tariff-rollback commitments while holding current tariffs as the bargaining chip. (Event timeline 2019-09-05 through 2019-09-13; country health fed funds, DGS10, DTWEXBGS, UMCSENT; web: CNBC 'Trump delays tariff hikes,' Reuters/NDTV talks reporting, farm-belt coverage.)
